facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square to take part in the 'March of Millions' march.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he walked down Yakimanka Street to Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he passed the metal detectors at Bolotnaya Square and joined other protestors in front of the stage, where a rock group was performing.
According to the applicant, he was both angered and scared by the actions of the police and actively resisted.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant, together with other unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder, tore off Police Officer K.'s anti-riot helmet.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant punched Police Officer K.'s head at least once and kicked Police Officer K. on the body at least once when the latter was lying on the ground.
The applicant was eventually seized by four police officers and escorted to a police car, which took him to a police station.

The applicant was sentenced by the Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow to detention of twenty-four hours for the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On 28 May 2012 the applicant was detained on suspicion of participation in acts of mass disorder on 6 May 2012.
On 28 May 2012 the applicant was detained on suspicion of committing violent acts against the police on 6 May 2012.
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Article 212 § 2 and Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and seven months' imprisonment.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riot, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of the acts of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the unidentified persons called those present at Bolotnaya Square to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that participants of the acts of mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them on various parts of their body.
According to the applicant, he was both angered and scared by the actions of the police and actively resisted.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant, together with other unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder, tore off Police Officer K.'s anti-riot helmet.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant punched Police Officer K.'s head at least once and kicked Police Officer K. on the body at least once when the latter was lying on the ground.

The applicant testified that he was scared, felt that his life was in danger, and while in a state of fury moved towards a police officer who happened to be Police Officer K., and then moved his leg towards the police officer who was getting up.
The applicant insisted at trial that he caused no injuries to the police officer and that his actions, provoked by panic, were taken in response to the events occurring around him.
